sections.heading: JPEG Compressor Online for Smaller and Optimized Photos
sections.body:
JPEG is one of the most commonly used image formats for digital photography. Cameras, smartphones, editing applications and websites use JPEG files because they can store detailed photographs in a relatively manageable file size.

Even so, some JPEG images may need further optimization before they can be uploaded, shared or added to a website. A high-resolution camera export can be larger than necessary for an email attachment, while a website may benefit from smaller image downloads.

The File Compresser JPEG Compressor helps you re-encode JPEG photographs with different quality settings. You can maintain the original display dimensions, choose a suitable compression level and enable resizing when smaller dimensions are needed. All processing takes place in your browser. Your selected photographs are not uploaded to File Compresser servers.

sections.heading: What Is a JPEG Compressor?
sections.body:
A JPEG compressor is a tool that changes how a JPEG image is encoded to reduce its file size. JPEG uses lossy compression, which means the encoding process can remove some image information. This helps reduce the amount of data required to store a photograph, but it can also affect visual quality.

The final result depends on the original photograph, its existing compression and the selected quality settings. File Compresser provides different options for people who want to reduce JPEG file size without making unnecessary changes to image dimensions.

sections.heading: JPG and JPEG: Is There Any Difference?
sections.body:
JPG and JPEG are two file extensions for the same image format. The term JPEG comes from the Joint Photographic Experts Group, the organization associated with the format's development. The shorter JPG extension became common because older operating systems used three-character file extensions.

Both extensions represent the same underlying image format. Changing a filename from .jpeg to .jpg does not reduce its size or improve its quality. Actual compression requires re-encoding the image with different settings. File Compresser uses the same image processing engine for its JPG and JPEG tools.

sections.heading: How to Compress JPEG Images Online
sections.body:
You can optimize a JPEG photograph in a few steps:

Open the JPEG Compressor page.

Start processing.
Compare the original and new file sizes.

The original photograph remains available on your device, allowing you to compare it with the processed copy.

sections.heading: Select a Suitable JPEG Quality Setting
sections.body: Not every photograph needs the same compression level. A small image for an online form may have different requirements from a high-quality product photograph.

sections.heading: Balanced
sections.body: Balanced offers a moderate approach to JPEG compression. It can be a useful starting point when you want to reduce file size while retaining a reasonable amount of visual detail.

sections.heading: High Quality
sections.body: High Quality prioritizes image detail over stronger size reduction. It may be appropriate for photographs where appearance is more important than achieving the smallest output.

sections.heading: Maximum
sections.body: Maximum uses a stronger compression trade-off to prioritize a smaller output. Check the final image carefully because fine details and textures may change.

sections.heading: Target Size
sections.body: Target Size attempts to create an image within a selected maximum number of bytes. The tool tests actual encodes instead of relying on an estimated file size. If no supported result meets the selected maximum, it reports that the target was not met. A very restrictive target can affect the quality of a photograph, so always check whether the output remains suitable for its intended use.

sections.heading: Why Should You Optimize JPEG Photographs?
sections.body: JPEG optimization can be useful in several everyday situations.

sections.heading: Website Image Optimization
sections.body: Website owners often use JPEG photographs on product pages, service pages, galleries and blog articles. Reducing unnecessary image data can help lower the total size of a web page. However, image compression should be combined with suitable image dimensions, responsive delivery and other website performance improvements.

sections.heading: Online Form Uploads
sections.body: Some online portals have strict image size requirements. A JPEG compressor can help prepare photographs for applications, registrations and other digital forms.

sections.heading: Email and File Sharing
sections.body: Smaller JPEG attachments can be easier to send and receive. This is especially useful when you need to share several photographs in one email.

sections.heading: Product and Business Photography
sections.body: Online stores and business websites often use many product photographs. Optimizing these files can help reduce storage requirements and the amount of data visitors download.

sections.heading: Does JPEG Compression Affect Image Quality?
sections.body:
JPEG compression is lossy, so re-encoding can change the original pixels. The amount of visible change depends on the selected quality setting. Strong compression may affect fine textures, color transitions, faces, small lettering and detailed edges.

A higher quality setting generally retains more detail, but it may create a larger output. For important photographs, compare both versions at the same scale. Keep the original file for future editing, printing or archiving. Repeatedly compressing an already compressed JPEG is not recommended. It can introduce additional artifacts without providing a useful reduction in file size.

sections.heading: Can You Resize JPEG Images?
sections.body:
Yes. File Compresser provides an optional resizing control.

By default, the original display dimensions are maintained. If you need a smaller photograph for a website, email or upload form, you can enable resizing and enter a maximum width or height.

The aspect ratio is preserved, and smaller images are not enlarged.

Resizing and compression are different processes. Resizing changes the pixel dimensions, while JPEG compression changes the way the image information is stored.

sections.heading: What Happens to Image Metadata?
sections.body:
Re-encoding can normalize image colors to sRGB and remove some metadata. Camera photographs may also contain EXIF information, such as camera details and orientation data. An unchanged original retains its existing bytes and metadata. If metadata is important to your workflow, keep a separate original before processing.

Also, remember that removing metadata during image compression is not a substitute for reviewing privacy information in the original file.

sections.heading: Private JPEG Processing Without Uploads
sections.body: File Compresser uses browser-based processing, so selected JPEG photographs remain on your device during compression. There is no need to upload personal photographs to an external compression server. The website loads the required processing code, and your device performs the image operation. The tool supports files up to 50 MB each, with a queue limit of 500 files and 300 MB total. Device memory and image dimensions can affect processing performance.
